title: Redis vs Valkey vs Dragonfly
deck: Three in-memory key-value stores tested across SET/GET throughput, pipelining, and memory efficiency with memtier_benchmark.

limitations: KeyDB omitted: the project is effectively unmaintained (last release 2023, open issues unresolved).

Each engine runs at its default threading configuration — single-threaded I/O for Redis and Valkey, multi-threaded for Dragonfly. This is intentional: the comparison measures what you get out of the box, not a hand-tuned configuration.

Local runs use a single-host topology where client and server share the same machine's resources. Network latency and CPU contention differ from a dedicated two-host setup. Cloud runs on separate instances eliminate this.
No clustering or replication — all tests target a single standalone instance.
No TLS overhead measured in this benchmark.

Eviction policy: Redis/Valkey use allkeys-lru (sampled LRU); Dragonfly uses --cache_mode (DASH-based eviction) since it does not expose maxmemory-policy as a CLI flag. The algorithms differ internally, which may affect eviction fairness under memory pressure.
